Study 7 · electromagnetics · no current

Open-circuit electromagnetics

With no current in the windings, the magnets alone set the flux linkage. That gives the back-EMF constant (the blind prediction for ORNL) and answers REQ-M1: if the inverter stops switching at top speed, does the motor's own voltage stay under the 500 V bus?

REQ-M1 fails, about twice over. The line-to-line back-EMF peak at 6000 rpm is about 1000-1030 V against the 500 V bus. That is expected for an interior-magnet design: above base speed the drive depends on field weakening, and a fault at top speed needs protection. The flux-linkage harmonics add 9.5 % to the peak over the fundamental on our machine, and 13 % on Pyleecan's, whose wider slots make the field less sinusoidal.

Method

  • 2D magnetostatic FEMM solves through Pyleecan, at 1000 rpm over one electrical period in 48 steps, using the machine's angular and time periodicity.
  • λ1 is the mean fundamental amplitude of the three phase flux linkages. The back-EMF constant is √3 ωe λ1 / √2 at 1000 rpm, with 4 pole pairs.
  • The peak at 6000 rpm is the largest |eab| from a spectral derivative of φa − φb, harmonics included, scaled by the speed ratio.
  • Mesh fineness divides all of Pyleecan's FEMM mesh sizes (at fineness 1: air gap 0.25 mm, rotor iron 1.94 mm, magnets 3.9 mm, teeth 4.3 mm, yoke 4.8 mm).

Checks on every point

CheckWhat is comparedLimitWhy
Phase symmetrySpread of the three phases' fundamental flux linkage, over the mean≤ 1e-3A wrong winding or periodicity breaks the balance.
Phase shiftLargest departure of the phase shifts from 120°≤ 0.5°Same, for the winding layout.
Winding theoryFlux linkage from FEMM's air-gap field, 2 N kw1 B1 R L / p, against FEMM's integral over the coils≤ 2 %An independent second route to the same number. Model-form differences (mid-gap sampling, slot openings, leakage) keep it near 0.5 %.
Open-circuit torqueMean torque with no current, over the rated 400 N m≤ 1e-3No net torque can come from magnets alone.
Time resolutionAt least 48 steps per electrical periodvaliditySettled in the prototype: 48 and 96 steps agree.
Mesh convergence (run level)GCI on the flux linkage and on the requirement metric, three meshes≤ 1 %A failed GCI withholds the requirement verdict on that run.

Back-EMF across the mesh studies

Both machines change by under 0.05 % between fineness 4 and 8. The step between them is the design-input correction: the wider air gap alone lowers the back-EMF 0.41 % (hollow marker), then the drawing's narrower slot raises it 1.4 %, because the wider teeth saturate less.

Case record: predictions before the run, results after
Study 7, first case: the 2004 Toyota Prius traction motor at open circuit (no current), Pyleecan + FEMM.

Decision this case informs: if the inverter stops switching at top speed (a fault), the magnets alone drive the
phase voltage: the "uncontrolled generator" condition. Does the motor's line-to-line back-EMF at its maximum speed
stay within the 500 V maximum bus voltage, or must the drive rely on active field weakening and protection? It
also fixes the back-EMF constant that the blind ORNL validation will compare against later (BACKLOG, study 7).

Design inputs: Pyleecan's Toyota_Prius.json (master 1e940df). Spot-checked against ORNL/TM-2004/137 (design report):
3.3 in stack exactly; series winding (2004); 200-500 V boosted bus; 400 N m peak torque. Not yet confirmed: the
diameters and air gap (in the report's figures). Assumptions: generic NdFeB magnet (Br 1.24 T at 20 C, recoil
permeability 1.05), M400-50A laminations (0.5 mm; the real ones are 0.36 mm; irrelevant at open circuit except
through the B-H curve).

Prototype (hand runs before this case): flux-linkage fundamental 0.20907 Wb at 48 and at 96 steps per electrical
  period (time resolution settled; 24 steps per mechanical revolution had given only 6 per electrical period);
  default and doubled mesh fineness agree to 1e-4; winding theory from the air-gap field 0.6-0.7 % above FEMM's
  coil integration; cogging torque mean 0.07 N m.

Predictions, written BEFORE the evidence run (and before any ORNL performance data has been opened):
  P1 Every point check passes on every mesh: phases within 1e-3 of each other and 120 deg apart, winding theory
     within 1 %, open-circuit torque under 1e-3 of the rated 400 N m.
  P2 Flux-linkage fundamental 0.2091 Wb, back-EMF 107.25 V line-to-line rms per 1000 rpm, mesh GCI under 0.1 %.
     This is the blind prediction for the ORNL comparison.
  P3 Line-to-line back-EMF peak at 6000 rpm about 910-930 V (the fundamental alone gives 910 V): REQ-M1 FAILS by
     about 80 %. Expected for this interior-PM design: it relies on field weakening above base speed.

Smoke test (scratch, mesh fineness 1, before the evidence run): every check passes (phase symmetry 1.8e-4, phase
  shift 0.004 deg, winding theory 0.54 %, open-circuit torque 2e-5 of rated). lambda1 0.20906 Wb, 107.253 V per
  1000 rpm (P2 held). The line-to-line peak at 6000 rpm is 1027 V, not 910-930: the flux-linkage harmonics add 13 %
  to the peak over the fundamental, more than the few percent assumed. P3 revised to about 1030 V; the verdict
  (REQ-M1 fails) is unchanged.

Results (run 20261121-194454_motor_prius_oc_mesh): every point check passes on every mesh (15/15). Line-to-line peak at
  6000 rpm 1026.7 / 1028.3 / 1028.0 V at mesh fineness 1 / 2 / 4 (oscillatory, uncertainty 0.10 %): REQ-M1 VERIFIED
  FAIL, about twice the 500 V bus. The drive depends on field weakening and fault protection at high speed (P3 as
  revised held). Flux-linkage fundamental 0.20906 / 0.20884 / 0.20864 Wb: monotone but observed order 0.19,
  extrapolated 0.20722; GCI 0.85 % passes the 1 % limit, but such a low order suggests the global refinement barely
  reaches what matters (likely the saturated rotor bridges). P2's GCI under 0.1 % MISSED. Revised blind prediction,
  still before any ORNL performance data is opened: back-EMF 107.0 V rms line-to-line per 1000 rpm at the finest
  mesh, with up to about 1 % attributable to the mesh (about 106 V extrapolated). Next: refine the bridges locally
  and check the order recovers. Solve times 14 / 28 / 101 s.

Case record: predictions before the run, results after
Study 7, open circuit, mesh study revision 1: mesh fineness 2 / 4 / 8. Same model, requirement and tolerances as
motor_prius_oc_mesh.toml; read it for the background and the first results.

Why: run 20261121-194454 verified REQ-M1 (fail, 1028 V) but the flux-linkage fundamental converged at order 0.19
(0.20906 / 0.20884 / 0.20864 Wb), too low to trust its extrapolation. Pyleecan's FEMM mesh sizes (comp_FEMM_dict, at
fineness 1): rotor iron 1.94 mm, magnets 3.9 mm, air gap 0.25 mm, stator teeth 4.3 mm, stator yoke 4.8 mm, all
divided by the fineness. The rotor bridges beside the magnets are 1-1.5 mm wide: under one element at fineness 1, so
that level is probably outside the asymptotic range. As in the strap and CFD studies, drop it and add a finer one.

Predictions, written BEFORE the run (still before any ORNL performance data has been opened):
  P1 Every point check passes on every mesh.
  P2 The flux-linkage fundamental keeps falling slowly: about 0.2088 / 0.2086 / 0.2085 Wb; observed order 0.5-1.5;
     GCI under 1 %. Back-EMF at fineness 8 about 106.9-107.0 V per 1000 rpm.
  P3 REQ-M1 unchanged: about 1028 V, a verified fail.
  P4 If the order stays below 0.5, the bridges need local refinement (FEMM_dict_enforced), not more global fineness.

Results (run 20261121-194926_motor_prius_oc_mesh_r1): every point check passes on every mesh (15/15). Flux-linkage
  fundamental 0.20884 / 0.20864 / 0.20859 Wb at fineness 2 / 4 / 8: monotone, observed order 1.95, extrapolated
  0.208568, GCI 0.01 %. P2 held and better: order near the design value once the coarsest level was dropped.
  BLIND PREDICTION, final, before any ORNL performance data is opened: back-EMF 107.0 V rms line-to-line per
  1000 rpm at 20 C (107.009 V at fineness 8), mesh uncertainty 0.01 %.
  Line-to-line peak at 6000 rpm 1028.28 / 1028.05 / 1027.45 V: spread 0.08 % but the differences grow (R = 2.67),
  so the GCI gives no estimate and REQ-M1 is formally withheld on this run. The peak carries the flux linkage's high
  harmonics, resolved by 48 steps per period, and so tiny mesh-to-mesh noise. Run 20261121-194454 verified it (fail,
  uncertainty 0.10 %). The margin is about 105 % over the 500 V limit, so the verdict is not in doubt. If needed, a
  later revision would measure that noise floor (time steps, mesh jitter) BEFORE rerunning, as the clevis study did.
  Solve times 27 s / 103 s / 15 min.

Case record: predictions before the run, results after
Study 7, open circuit on OUR machine definition: the 2004 Prius rebuilt from ORNL/TM-2005/33 Fig. 21
(models/motor/Toyota_Prius_ORNL.json, made by models/motor/build_prius_ornl.py, which records the source of every
dimension). Same model, requirement, sweep and tolerances as motor_prius_oc_mesh_r1.toml (Pyleecan's own
Toyota_Prius.json); read that case for the background.

What the rebuild changed (2026-11-21), dimension by dimension against Pyleecan's file:
  - radii: stator OD, bore, rotor OD and ID within 0.012 mm, but the air gap is 0.7747 mm against 0.750 mm;
  - slot opening 1.93 mm (same), tooth tip 1.016 mm (+1.6 %);
  - the slot itself is much narrower: 3.15 mm at the shoulder (Pyleecan 5.0, -37 %), round end 5.64 mm diameter
    (Pyleecan 8.0, -30 %), depth 33.53 mm (Pyleecan 34.29). Slot area 144.9 mm^2 against 217.5 mm^2. The drawing's
    slot inset and its main-view vector outline agree (0.125 in just above the tooth tip, 0.218 in at r = 4.35 in,
    end at r = 4.51 in, tooth 0.300 in near the bore, which is the drawing's own label), so the published source
    wins, as agreed.
  - unchanged, no published source in hand yet: magnet pockets, magnets, materials, winding, stack.
Scratch sensitivity before this case (BACKLOG, 21:45): the radii alone (air gap 0.775 mm) lowered the back-EMF
0.41 %, to 106.59 V per 1000 rpm at fineness 4. The slot change had not been tried.

Why the slot should matter even at open circuit: the last verified run's air-gap fundamental is 0.893 T. Spread over
Pyleecan's 5.55 mm tooth at the bore (pitch 10.55 mm) that is about 1.70 T, past the knee of M400-50A; over the
drawing's 7.40 mm tooth it is about 1.27 T. Less tooth saturation means less magnet MMF lost in the iron.

Predictions, written BEFORE the run (and still before any ORNL performance data has been opened):
  P1 Every point check passes on every mesh (phase symmetry, 120 deg shifts, winding theory within 2 %, zero mean
     open-circuit torque).
  P2 The flux linkage converges as on Pyleecan's machine: monotone, order 1-2.5, GCI under 1 %.
  P3 The back-EMF RISES against the radii-only 106.6 V: by 2-6 %, central estimate about +3 %, so about 110 V rms
     line-to-line per 1000 rpm (range 108.5-113). If it moves by under 1 %, the teeth were not the bottleneck and the
     1.7 T estimate above is wrong (the tooth widens quickly away from the bore).
  P4 REQ-M1 stays a fail, near 1060 V (scales with the back-EMF).
  P5 Solve times close to the r1 run (27 s / 103 s / 15 min), maybe slower while the FSI1 run shares the CPU.
If P3 holds, this machine replaces Pyleecan's as the design input, and the blind prediction moves with it, with
the reason written down here (a design-input correction, not tuning: no test data has been seen).

Results (run 20261121-215053_motor_prius_ornl_oc_mesh): verification PASS.
  P1 HELD: every point check passes on every mesh (15/15); winding theory 0.30 % (0.55 % on Pyleecan's machine).
  P2 PARTLY: flux-linkage fundamental 0.210853 / 0.210695 / 0.210591 Wb at fineness 2 / 4 / 8, monotone, GCI 0.12 %
     (passes 1 %), but observed order 0.60, under the predicted 1-2.5. Extrapolated 0.210389 Wb.
  P3 MISSED: back-EMF 108.17 / 108.09 / 108.04 V per 1000 rpm. Against the radii-only scratch at the same fineness 4
     (106.59 V) that is +1.4 %, under the predicted 2-6 %; against Pyleecan's machine at fineness 8 (107.01 V), +0.96 %
     (the air gap's -0.41 % and the slot's +1.4 % together). The narrower slot does raise the flux, as reasoned, but
     less: the 1.7 T estimate takes the tooth width at the bore, and the teeth widen quickly outward.
  P4 MISSED in direction, verdict unchanged: line-to-line peak at 6000 rpm 1004.2 / 1004.0 / 1003.9 V, DOWN 2.3 % from
     1027.5 V while the fundamental went up. The harmonics shrank: the peak is now 9.5 % over the fundamental's
     (sqrt 2 x 108.04 x 6 = 916.7 V), against 13.2 % on Pyleecan's machine. Monotone, GCI 0.02 %: REQ-M1 VERIFIED FAIL
     on this run, about twice the 500 V bus.
  P5: solve times 20 s / 72 s / 10 min, faster than r1 despite the FSI1 run.
  Decision: this machine replaces Pyleecan's as the design input, by the agreed rule (the published source wins), not
  because of P3. BLIND PREDICTION, revised for a design-input correction, before any ORNL performance data is opened:
  back-EMF 108.0 V rms line-to-line per 1000 rpm at 20 C (108.04 V at fineness 8), mesh uncertainty 0.12 %. Still
  Pyleecan's: magnet pockets, magnet and lamination materials.

Study 7, open circuit, revision 1 of our machine: the rotor and magnets now from published sources too (BACKLOG,
"magnet pockets and magnets, sources found"). Same model, sweep, requirement and tolerances as
motor_prius_ornl_oc_mesh.toml; read it for the stator rebuild and the first results (108.04 V per 1000 rpm).

What changed in models/motor/Toyota_Prius_ORNL.json (build_prius_ornl.py records each source):
  - pocket (and magnet) thickness 6.50 -> 6.78 mm, measured on Fig. 21's vector outline (8 poles, sd 0.05 mm); the
    V angle and apex depth already matched;
  - bridge 1.50 -> 1.45 mm (ORNL/TM-2004/120 Table 5.3);
  - magnet Br 1.24 -> 1.243 T and recoil permeability 1.05 -> 1.129, digitized from ORNL/TM-2004/137 Fig. 14, ORNL's
    measured line of a Prius magnet sample (opened by the user's decision, 2026-11-21: a material property).
Scratch sensitivity at fineness 4 before the change (one at a time): pocket 6.78 mm +0.42 %; Br 1.12 T -11.3 % (the
reason Fig. 14 was needed); magnet 5.31 mm -2.38 % and 19.24 mm wide +2.01 % (TM-2004/120's size, not adopted).

Predictions, written BEFORE the run (no ORNL measured data opened):
  P1 Every point check passes on every mesh.
  P2 Back-EMF 107.9 V per 1000 rpm (range 107.3-108.6): pocket +0.42 %, Br +0.24 %, bridge about +0.1 %, and the
     higher recoil permeability about -0.8 % (a simple magnetic circuit: B ~ Br / (1 + mu_r g_eff / l_m), with
     mu_r g_eff / l_m about 0.14 to 0.15).
  P3 GCI under 1 %, monotone; REQ-M1 a verified fail near 1003 V.
  P4 Solve times about 20 s / 70 s / 10 min.

Results (run 20261121-223608_motor_prius_ornl_oc_mesh_r1): verification PASS.

Case record: predictions before the run, results after
Study 7, open circuit, revision 2 of our machine: the pocket's extra thickness moved to the air-gap side. Same model,
sweep, requirement and tolerances as motor_prius_ornl_oc_mesh_r1.toml; read it (and motor_prius_ornl_oc_mesh.toml)
for the background.

Why: r1 grew the pocket inward (HoleM50's H3 alone). Fig. 21 is stretched 1.1 % in x in the PDF (its rotor OD outline
is an ellipse, x/y 1.0114); corrected, the drawing's inner edge matches Pyleecan's (inner apex 17.76 against 17.78 mm
below the OD) and its outer apex is 10.65 mm deep against Pyleecan's 10.96. So: H0 10.65 mm, H3 6.80 mm, W0 41.21 mm
(keeps the 17.4 deg arm angle). Bridge, magnet Br and recoil permeability as in r1. The machine file also no longer
carries Pyleecan's absolute material paths (metadata only).

Predictions, written BEFORE the run (no ORNL measured data opened):
  P1 Every point check passes on every mesh.
  P2 Back-EMF slightly above r1 (the magnet's outer face 0.3 mm nearer the gap, less flux lost to the rotor iron
     above it): about +0.2 % (0 to +0.5 %) on r1's finest-mesh value.
  P3 GCI under 1 %; REQ-M1 a verified fail near 1010 V.
Its finest-mesh back-EMF becomes the blind prediction.

Case record: predictions before the run, results after
Study 7, open circuit, revision 3 of our machine: the laminations are now M330-35A, the study's single stand-in
steel (user's decision 2026-11-22 ~00:40, BACKLOG). Same geometry, magnets, model, sweep, requirement and tolerances
as motor_prius_ornl_oc_mesh_r2.toml; read it (and r1, and motor_prius_ornl_oc_mesh.toml) for the background.

Why: until now the electromagnetics used the M400-50A B-H curve (0.5 mm) that came with Pyleecan's file and was never
chosen, while the overspeed check and the loss data use M330-35A (0.35 mm, closer to ORNL's 0.36 mm). ORNL gives the
thickness but not the grade. models/motor/build_prius_ornl.py (--steel, default M330-35A) now writes Tata Steel's
M330-35A typical B-H curve (50 Hz, 0.1-1.8 T) into both laminations, extended above 1.8 T by our extrapolation
(saturation polarization 2.0 T, slope-continuous; build_prius_ornl._tail), with M330-35A's density, resistivity and
modulus. A design-input correction made before the ORNL data is opened, with this written reason. r2 (M400-50A) stays
as the "inherited steel" side of the sensitivity.

The two curves: M330-35A needs much less field below 1.7 T (1.0 T: 114 against 250 A/m; 1.3 T: 242 against 950;
1.5 T: 1027 against 2450; 1.7 T: 5409 against 6700). Above about 28 kA/m our M330-35A tail gives the lower flux
density (100 kA/m: 2.105 against 2.20 T).

Predictions, written BEFORE the run (no ORNL measured data opened; r2's results not yet read):
  P1 Every point check passes on every mesh.
  P2 Back-EMF about +2.0 % on r2's finest-mesh value (range +1.0 to +3.5 %). Magnetic circuit: B ~ Br / (1 + x), x the
     external MMF drop over the magnet MMF, about 0.14 (r1). Iron is roughly 30 % of that drop with M400-50A (teeth
     near 1.5-1.6 T over 33.5 mm, yoke near 1.3-1.4 T); M330-35A about halves it, so x falls to about 0.12:
     1.14 / 1.12 = +1.8 %. The bridges, saturated, carry slightly less leakage flux on the lower tail: +0.1 to +0.5 %.
  P3 GCI under 1 %; REQ-M1 a verified fail, about 2 % above r2's value (near 1030 V).
  P4 Solve times as r2 (about 20 s / 80 s / 9 min).
Its finest-mesh back-EMF becomes the blind prediction (with M330-35A as the stand-in steel).

blind predictions become ranges. This grade is the lower-loss side: a higher-silicon grade that needs more field above 1.3 T (1.4 T: 642 against 428 A/m; 1.5 T: 1810 against 1027; 1.7 T: 7290 against 5409; 1.8 T: 11700 against 9677), about the same below.

     changed the iron MMF by about 90 A (teeth near 1.5 T over 33.5 mm, yoke near 1.3 T over about 60 mm) and moved the
     back-EMF +1.08 %; M330-35A -> M250-35A adds about 29 A (mostly the teeth), so about a third of that, negative.

     finest (110.884 V) against -0.35 % (-0.7 to -0.1 %). The estimate charged the whole difference to the teeth near
     1.5 T, where M250-35A needs more field. Two things push the other way and outweighed it: below about 1.15 T
     M250-35A needs LESS field (1.0 T: 107 against 114 A/m; 0.5 T: 53 against 64), where most of the open-circuit
     iron runs; and in deep saturation its tail carries slightly less flux (50 kA/m: 2.011 against 2.021 T; 100 kA/m:
     2.101 against 2.105 T), so the saturated bridges leak a little less. Either means the open-circuit teeth run
     below the assumed 1.5 T, which agrees with r3's P2 landing at the low end of its range. Not separated here
